cr_rationale: Life first: the escape stair is compromised and occupancy is unknown in a block of up to 13 storeys. We send 5 pumps, the ALP and the rescue tender (PPV for the only stair), with 3 ambulances and an RRV. The area's only critical care car and HART stay uncommitted until persons are reported. One MCU and one drone serve the whole scene. The public order van is dropped. The roads policing unit is kept because an active RTC sits on the Duke Street access route. Fire's 100/250 m cordons and 150 m debris zone apply as lead agency.

routing.rationale: High-rise residential fire at Park Hill flats (up to 13 storeys), severity 4. Smoke in the shared stairwell means the escape route may be compromised. Other residents may still be inside, and the number trapped is unknown. Fire leads for firefighting, search and rescue, and evacuation of the block. Ambulance attends for possible smoke inhalation among residents still inside or evacuating. Caller's household has evacuated with no casualties reported. Police attend for cordon, traffic and crowd control, and to support evacuation of a large multi-occupancy block. No weapons reported. No other active or pending incidents competing for units.

resource_requests.justification: High-rise residential fire. The minimum attendance is 4 pumps regardless of initial reports [pre_determined_attendance#High-rise residential fire]. Severity 4 also requires 4 pumps on its own [pre_determined_attendance#Dwelling fire]. Crews are needed for firefighting from a bridgehead, BA entry control, stairwell search and rescue, and water supply.

The minimum high-rise attendance includes 1 ALP [pre_determined_attendance#High-rise residential fire]. Park Hill has up to 13 storeys. The ALP is needed for external rescue of occupants on upper floors cut off by the smoke-logged stairwell, and as an external water tower.

Occupants may still be inside and the shared escape stairwell is smoke-logged. A 5th pump adds BA crews for search and rescue and for door-to-door evacuation if the incident commander moves from stay-put to simultaneous evacuation. This follows the add-1-pump-if-persons-reported guidance [pre_determined_attendance#Dwelling fire].
Provides specialist rescue equipment, extra BA cylinders and smoke ventilation (PPV) to clear the stairwell escape route in a large multi-storey complex where occupants may still be inside.

Severity 4 requires a Level 2 incident commander [pre_determined_attendance#Dwelling fire]. The command unit supports multi-agency command, BA entry control tallies, the evacuation strategy decision log and floor-by-floor tracking of occupants.
Aerial and thermal view of the building faces. It helps locate the fire floor, track external spread and smoke movement, and spot occupants at windows or balconies.

mission_details.summary: A fire is reported in a residential block at Park Hill flats (up to 13 storeys) with smoke in the stairwell. The caller's household has evacuated, but other occupants may still be inside and the shared escape route is compromised. High-rise attendance is mobilised: 5 pumps, an ALP, a rescue tender, a command unit and a drone. The incident is run under Level 2 command.
tactical_plan: First pump: confirm the fire floor and location, and establish entry control at the building entrance.
Set up a bridgehead two floors below the fire floor [pre_determined_attendance#High-rise residential fire]. Charge the dry/wet riser and run firefighting jets from the bridgehead.
Commit BA teams to search the fire floor and the floors above, prioritising the stairwell and flats adjacent to the fire.

Incident commander to decide stay-put vs simultaneous evacuation early, based on stairwell smoke-logging and fire spread, and review it continuously. Evacuation must be considered because the escape route is compromised.
Pitch the ALP on the affected face for external rescue from windows or balconies and as a water tower if needed.
Rescue tender to use PPV to clear the stairwell once the fire is isolated.
Enforce the 100 m inner cordon (BA-equipped crews only) and a 150 m debris exclusion zone on affected faces.
Use the drone to monitor the building faces for external spread and trapped occupants.
Monitor for fire damage beyond one floor. If found, set a collapse zone of 1.5 times building height (about 60 m) [scene_safety_and_cordons#Collapse zone].
hazards_identified: Smoke-logged common stairwell compromising the single escape route
Occupants possibly still inside on upper floors
Multi-storey building up to 13 storeys: vertical and external fire spread risk
Falling debris and glass from upper floors
Possible failure of fire compartmentation in the older concrete deck-access structure
Heat and smoke exposure for crews, long internal travel distances, BA duration limits
safety_notes: Other agencies must not enter while fire is active; entry is prohibited and only BA crews may cross the inner cordon [scene_safety_and_cordons#Inner cordon and entry control].
All personnel entering must be logged at the entry control point.
Keep falling-debris exclusion on affected faces, with covered or protected entry routes into the building.
Rotate BA crews and keep emergency BA teams at the bridgehead.
Scene entry may be downgraded to 'controlled' only when the incident commander judges escorted entry safe.

resource_requests.justification: Fire in a residential block of up to 13 storeys with a smoke-logged shared stairwell. The caller has evacuated, but occupants may still be inside. Fire rescues are likely to produce smoke-inhalation casualties. Two ambulances will stand by at the forward rendezvous point to treat and convey anyone fire crews bring to the cordon. Self-evacuated residents will also need assessment.

The first clinician on scene liaises with the fire incident commander and triages evacuated residents at the assembly point. This frees the ambulances for conveyance. The unit is of little value if it arrives after the early triage phase.

Casualties rescued from smoke-logged floors may have severe smoke inhalation, airway burns or carbon monoxide or cyanide toxicity. These patients may need advanced airway management and critical care support before conveyance.

Precautionary only. Under [major_incidents_and_hazardous_areas#HART (Hazardous Area Response Team)], only HART may work inside an inner cordon. If fire escalates to persons reported or multiple casualties, HART can treat at or inside the inner cordon. Upgrade the priority if multiple casualties are confirmed.

mission_details.summary: Fire with a smoke-logged stairwell in a multi-storey residential block at Park Hill flats. Fire service is the lead agency. No casualties have been reported yet, but occupants may still be inside. Ambulance will stand by at the cordon to treat smoke-inhalation and burns casualties and to assess self-evacuated residents.
tactical_plan: Rapid response vehicle clinician reports to the fire incident commander at the rendezvous point and takes the ambulance commander role until relieved.
Set up the ambulance loading point and casualty clearing area upwind, outside the inner cordon, at the location agreed with fire.
Triage and assess evacuated residents at the assembly point, with priority for smoke-exposed, elderly, paediatric and respiratory-compromised patients.
Ambulance crews do not enter the building or the inner cordon. Fire crews bring rescued casualties to the cordon.
Treat smoke inhalation with high-flow oxygen. Suspect carbon monoxide or cyanide toxicity in any patient with reduced consciousness.

Convey adults with burns or significant inhalation injury to Northern General Hospital (major trauma and burns). Convey children to Sheffield Children's Hospital. Royal Hallamshire Hospital takes minor smoke exposure overflow.
Escalate to a major incident declaration, request more ambulances and upgrade HART to priority 1 if multiple casualties or persons reported are confirmed.

safety_notes: Ambulance crews must not enter a scene declared unsafe by fire. Casualties come to the cordon.

resource_requests.justification: Set and hold the outer cordon around the Park Hill block, which must enclose any fire evacuation zone. Close and divert roads to keep appliance access clear. Manage, account for and reassure evacuated residents. Log access at the cordon.
Run road closures and diversions on the arterial routes next to Park Hill and the Sheffield station area. Keep the routes for fire appliances, aerial platforms and ambulances clear.

Provide aerial overwatch of the multi-storey block to support fire command situational awareness and track fire spread across the facade and roof. Also monitor crowds at the cordon. Footage arriving late adds less value to the early tactical picture.
Provide a co-located police command point at the multi-agency RVP, in line with JESIP. This is a large residential complex with many evacuees and a likely prolonged incident.
Supply extra officers to manage a potentially large number of displaced residents and onlookers. They will also support the cordon perimeter and the welfare and rest-centre arrangements.

mission_details.summary:
Fire is the lead agency at a high-rise residential fire at Park Hill flats, with smoke in the stairwell. Police will:
- set and hold the outer cordon
- manage traffic
- keep emergency access routes open
- account for and support evacuated residents
- protect the scene for a possible fire or crime investigation.

Police will not enter the building.
tactical_plan: 1. Confirm the inner cordon and evacuation zone with the Fire Incident Commander on arrival. Set the outer cordon at about 200 m and widen it if fire extends the evacuation.
2. Establish a single multi-agency RVP just outside the outer cordon. Co-locate the police commander with Fire and Ambulance commanders (JESIP).
3. Close the roads next to the block and set up diversions. Keep Duke Street and South Street clear for appliances and aerial platforms.
4. Gather evacuated residents at a safe holding point. Record names and flat numbers and pass any reports of missing occupants to Fire straight away.
5. Log all access at the cordon. Keep members of the public and press outside the outer cordon.
6. Deploy the drone for overwatch and share the feed with the Fire IC.
7. Keep an open mind on the cause. Note witnesses, CCTV and anyone acting suspiciously, and hand over to a joint fire/police investigation if arson is indicated.
8. Work with the local authority on a rest centre for displaced residents.

findings: Every requested essential resource was sent, and first units from fire, ambulance and police arrived within 3 minutes, well inside their targets.
Five fire engines, an aerial ladder platform and a rescue tender were sent for a possible 13-storey building with a smoke-filled stairwell.
Four non-essential units were trimmed from the original request, with no effect on essential cover.
No one is confirmed trapped, but other occupants are not yet accounted for, so the evacuee roll-call and fire search results need confirming.
evaluation.headline: Fire crews rush to Park Hill flats as smoke fills stairwell
evaluation.dek: Residents fled a fire at Park Hill flats; five fire engines, a high-reach ladder, three ambulances and police were sent, with the first crews arriving in under three minutes.
